name: TutorHelper Bookings
author: teachallaboutit

sections.description:
TutorHelper Bookings is a WordPress booking plugin created specifically for independent tutors and tuition providers.

It provides the Core tools needed to publish lesson availability, allow registered students to request available lessons, and manage those bookings from your own WordPress website.

Instead of sending students to a separate scheduling service, TutorHelper keeps your booking experience within the website you already manage.

Designed for tutors

TutorHelper Bookings follows a request-and-confirm workflow designed around private tuition:

  1. The tutor creates one or more Booking Types.
  2. The tutor publishes the dates and times they are available.
  3. A registered student chooses an available lesson and submits a booking request.
  4. The request appears in the TutorHelper Booking Hub as awaiting confirmation.
  5. The tutor reviews the request and confirms the lesson.
  6. The student can view the lesson from their TutorHelper student dashboard.
  7. TutorHelper sends the appropriate request, confirmation and cancellation emails throughout the process.

The free Core plugin does not require an external TutorHelper booking service.

Core features

  • Create and manage multiple Booking Types.
  • Set lesson duration and price information.
  • Configure online, telephone, in-person and custom lesson locations.
  • Set minimum booking notice for each Booking Type.
  • Enable or disable student cancellation for each Booking Type.
  • Set a minimum cancellation notice period.
  • Create recurring weekly tutor availability.
  • Restrict availability to selected Booking Types and locations.
  • Make date-specific changes to recurring availability.
  • Remove individual dates or ranges from recurring availability.
  • Prevent students from requesting unavailable or conflicting lesson times.
  • View lessons and availability through the TutorHelper Booking Hub calendar.
  • View the Booking Hub by week or month.
  • Create and edit tutor-entered bookings.
  • Confirm student lesson requests from the Booking Hub.
  • Allow registered students to request available lessons online.
  • Display the responsive booking form using a shortcode.
  • Give students a dashboard showing pending, upcoming, cancelled and previous lessons.
  • Allow students to cancel eligible lessons and provide a cancellation reason.
  • Allow tutors to cancel lessons and provide a reason to the student.
  • Keep cancelled lessons visible as part of the booking history.
  • Manage registered TutorHelper students from WordPress.
  • Send automatic lesson request, confirmation and cancellation emails.
  • Enable or disable individual Core email templates.
  • Edit the subject and message text of the fixed Core email templates.
  • Configure shared email sender, contact and privacy-policy details.
  • Configure the pages used for student booking, lesson management and login.
  • Use the standard WordPress login page or select a custom login page.
  • Configure the working currency used for Booking Type prices and new bookings.
  • Run TutorHelper Diagnostics to check whether the essential booking setup is ready.
  • Download diagnostic system information and TutorHelper technical logs when troubleshooting.
  • Store Core booking and availability information within the WordPress database.

Booking Shortcodes

Use the following shortcode to display the student lesson booking form:

[tutorhelper_student_booking]

Use the following shortcode to display the logged-in student’s lesson dashboard:

[tutorhelper_student_dashboard]

Students must be logged in with a registered TutorHelper student account to request lessons or view their lesson dashboard.

Student booking workflow

Student bookings are submitted as lesson requests.

A new student request is not automatically confirmed. The tutor can review the request from the TutorHelper Booking Hub and change its status to Confirmed.

TutorHelper Core is designed around individual lesson requests. Recurring booking requests, multiple simultaneous bookings and integrated online payments are not included in Core.

Booking Types

Booking Types describe the lessons or services you offer.

Each Booking Type can define information including:

  • Title and description.
  • Lesson duration.
  • Price information.
  • Available location types.
  • Location or joining details.
  • Minimum booking notice.
  • Whether student cancellation is allowed.
  • Minimum cancellation notice.
  • Whether the Booking Type can be requested through online booking.

Booking Types can be reordered and archived when they are no longer required.

Availability

TutorHelper Availability controls when students may request lessons.

You can create recurring weekly availability and then make changes to individual dates or date ranges when your normal timetable changes.

Availability can also be restricted to particular Booking Types or lesson locations.

TutorHelper checks existing bookings and tutor unavailability before allowing a student to request a lesson time.

Booking Hub

The TutorHelper Booking Hub provides a calendar-based view of your lessons and availability.

Tutors can use it to:

  • View bookings by week or month.
  • Review pending student lesson requests.
  • Confirm lesson requests.
  • Create tutor-entered bookings.
  • Edit upcoming bookings.
  • Cancel lessons.
  • Review cancelled lessons and cancellation reasons.
  • Work with Booking Types and Availability from the booking interface.

Student dashboard

The student dashboard gives logged-in students a simple view of their lessons.

It separates lessons into useful sections including:

  • Pending requests.
  • Upcoming lessons.
  • Cancelled lessons.
  • Previous lessons and booking history.

Where a Booking Type permits student cancellation and the required notice remains, the student can cancel the lesson from their dashboard and provide a cancellation reason.

Booking emails

TutorHelper Core includes fixed automatic email templates for the standard booking workflow.

These include messages for:

  • A new student lesson request sent to the tutor.
  • Confirmation that the student’s request was received.
  • A confirmed lesson.
  • A cancelled lesson.
  • A student cancellation notification sent to the tutor.

Core users can enable or disable these registered templates and edit their subject and message text.

The layout and template types themselves remain controlled by TutorHelper Core.

Emails are sent using the standard WordPress wp_mail() function. Actual email delivery can therefore be affected by the website’s hosting configuration or any SMTP or transactional email plugin in use.

TutorHelper Diagnostics

TutorHelper Diagnostics checks important parts of the Core booking setup and highlights anything that may need attention.

Checks include areas such as:

  • Database readiness.
  • Student booking and dashboard pages.
  • Active Booking Types.
  • Tutor availability.
  • Tutor configuration.
  • Email settings.
  • Privacy-policy configuration.

The Diagnostics screen also provides technical system information and TutorHelper log information that can be reviewed when troubleshooting.

Diagnostic information is not sent automatically to TutorHelper.

Privacy

TutorHelper Bookings stores information required to provide and manage lesson bookings.

Depending on how the plugin is used, this may include:

  • WordPress user IDs.
  • Student account information.
  • Student names.
  • Student email addresses.
  • Booking dates and times.
  • Booking Type information.
  • Lesson location and joining information.
  • Student booking notes.
  • Booking status.
  • Cancellation status and reasons.
  • Tutor and student relationships required to manage bookings.

Core booking and availability information is stored within the WordPress database.

TutorHelper Bookings does not automatically send booking information to an external TutorHelper booking service.

Automatic emails are sent through the WordPress wp_mail() system. Information contained within an email will therefore be processed by the website’s configured email-delivery system.

TutorHelper also maintains a limited technical diagnostic log. The logger is designed to record technical information rather than student names, email addresses or other unnecessary personal information.

Website owners are responsible for explaining how booking information is collected, processed, stored and retained within their own privacy policy and for complying with the privacy requirements that apply to their organisation.

TutorHelper Pro

TutorHelper Bookings Core is designed to remain useful as a standalone free plugin.

Additional TutorHelper Pro functionality may be available separately for tutors who require more advanced booking tools.

Planned advanced functionality may include features such as:

  • Recurring lesson bookings.
  • Multiple lesson bookings.
  • Integrated online payments.
  • More advanced Booking Type restrictions.
  • Term-time-only booking rules.
  • Additional booking automation.
  • More advanced booking management tools.
  • Extended email customisation, layouts and branding.

TutorHelper Bookings Core does not require TutorHelper Pro in order to provide its standard booking workflow.

Support

Support for the free plugin is available through the WordPress.org support forum.

TutorHelper documentation, tutorials and information about additional TutorHelper products are available from the TutorHelper website.

Video tutorials are also available through the TutorHelper YouTube channel.
sections.installation:
1. Install TutorHelper Bookings through the WordPress Plugins screen, or upload the plugin to your /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate TutorHelper Bookings.
  3. Open TutorHelper > Settings and review the Pages, Currency and Email settings.
  4. Create a WordPress page for student booking and add the [tutorhelper_student_booking] shortcode.
  5. Create a WordPress page for the student lesson dashboard and add the [tutorhelper_student_dashboard] shortcode.
  6. Select those pages under TutorHelper > Settings > Pages.
  7. Optionally select a custom student Login page. If none is selected, TutorHelper uses the standard WordPress login page.
  8. Open the TutorHelper Booking Hub and create at least one Booking Type.
  9. Add the dates and times that students may request under Availability.
  10. Ensure the students who should use online booking have registered TutorHelper student accounts.
  11. Open Tools > TutorHelper Diagnostics to check that the essential booking setup is ready.
  12. Test the booking process using a student account before publishing the booking page to students.
sections.faq:
Do students need a WordPress account?

Yes.

Students must be logged in with a registered TutorHelper student account to request a lesson or view their lesson dashboard.

This allows TutorHelper to associate bookings with the correct student and prevents anonymous lesson requests.

Is Tutor LMS required?

No.

TutorHelper Bookings is a standalone WordPress booking plugin and does not require Tutor LMS.

Does a student booking become confirmed immediately?

No.

A student submits a lesson request. The request is created as awaiting confirmation so that the tutor can review it from the Booking Hub.

The tutor can then confirm the lesson.

Can I create more than one type of lesson?

Yes.

You can create multiple Booking Types with different names, durations, prices, locations, notice periods and cancellation rules.

Can I offer both online and in-person lessons?

Yes.

Booking Types and Availability can support online, telephone, in-person and custom lesson locations.

Can I control how much notice students must give when booking?

Yes.

Each Booking Type has a minimum booking-notice setting.

Times that fall inside the minimum-notice period are not offered to students for online booking.

Can students cancel lessons?

Yes, where cancellation is enabled for the relevant Booking Type.

You can also configure how much notice the student must give before cancellation is no longer available.

Cancelled lessons remain part of the student’s booking history.

Can tutors cancel lessons?

Yes.

Tutors can cancel a lesson from the Booking Hub and provide a cancellation reason for the student.

Can students make recurring bookings?

Not in TutorHelper Bookings Core.

Core handles individual lesson requests. Recurring and multiple-booking functionality may be provided through additional TutorHelper functionality.

Does TutorHelper Bookings accept online payments?

TutorHelper Bookings Core does not process integrated online payments.

Price information can be stored against Booking Types and bookings, but the Core student booking workflow does not require or collect payment.

Integrated payment functionality may be available separately.

Can I edit the automatic emails?

Yes.

Core provides a fixed set of booking email templates. You can enable or disable individual templates and edit their subject and message text.

More advanced email layouts, branding and custom template functionality may be available separately.

How are booking emails sent?

Emails are sent using the standard WordPress wp_mail() function.

If your website has difficulty delivering WordPress emails, you may wish to configure a suitable SMTP or transactional email solution.

Can I use my own login page?

Yes.

You can select a Login page under TutorHelper > Settings > Pages.

If you leave this setting empty, TutorHelper uses the standard WordPress login page.

Does the plugin connect to an external booking service?

No.

TutorHelper Core booking and availability data is stored within your WordPress website.

What happens if I uninstall or delete the plugin?

TutorHelper Bookings intentionally keeps its booking, availability, settings and related data when the plugin is uninstalled.

This allows an existing TutorHelper booking setup and booking history to be restored if the plugin is installed again later.

Website owners remain responsible for deciding how long personal and booking information should be retained and for removing information when it is no longer required under their own privacy and data-retention obligations.

How can I check whether TutorHelper is configured correctly?

Open Tools > TutorHelper Diagnostics.

The readiness checks highlight important configuration items and provide technical information that may help with troubleshooting.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • Initial release of TutorHelper Bookings Core.
  • Added Booking Types with duration, pricing, location, booking-notice and cancellation settings.
  • Added recurring tutor Availability and date-specific availability changes.
  • Added weekly and monthly Booking Hub calendar views.
  • Added tutor-created booking management.
  • Added student lesson requests with tutor confirmation.
  • Added responsive student booking shortcode.
  • Added student dashboard shortcode with pending, upcoming, cancelled and previous lessons.
  • Added tutor and student cancellation workflows with cancellation reasons.
  • Added TutorHelper student management.
  • Added automatic lesson request, confirmation and cancellation emails.
  • Added editable Core email subjects and message text.
  • Added TutorHelper Pages, Currency and Email settings.
  • Added configurable student login-page support with WordPress login fallback.
  • Added TutorHelper Diagnostics and technical logging.
  • Added Core booking security, ownership and permission checks.
